svg.title: Keep the API layer close to the GPUs
svg.desc: Network latency. An AI gateway or geo-DNS sends each client to the API layer of its region. Two regions, region-a with most of the traffic and region-b with the rest, each have an API layer next to their GPU machines; the API layer probes every node and routes to the nearest replica, a short round trip. Only when the near replicas are busy does region-a's API layer use region-b's machines, a long round trip. Every response carries a Server-Timing header with route, queue, connect, net, engine and first-token time. Each API layer measures its own round trip to every node over the path it uses (tunnel or direct); routing prefers the nearest healthy replica until it gets busy, and placement puts replicas near the API layers that carry a deployment's traffic.
